## Background

The notification context is still a placeholder (#215), and the SWE5001 distributed shape needs `notification-svc` to consume cross-service events ([microservice-refactoring-plan.md](https://github.com/PPsyrius/iss-groupbuy-team8/blob/dev/docs/swe5001/microservice-refactoring-plan.md), [impl-backend-architecture.md](https://github.com/PPsyrius/iss-groupbuy-team8/blob/dev/docs/swe5001/impl-backend-architecture.md) WP-B6/B7). The SWE5001 presentation on 2026-10-21 focuses on a standard event-driven implementation and on scalability.

Design decisions from the 2026-10-11 discussion, to be recorded in backend ADR 0007 (#443):

- Transactional outbox → **one SNS topic** (filter policies on `eventType`) → **SQS queue per consumer + DLQ** (`maxReceiveCount = 5`) → idempotent consumer keyed on the envelope `eventId`.
- SNS is kept for real pub/sub and a live fan-out demo (notification queue + filtered audit queue); at course volume SNS/SQS stay within the free tier, so it adds effectively no cost.
- The transport is decoupled from the deployment topology (`blocbuy.events.transport = sqs | sns`): local, CI and the SWE5006 EC2 stack use ElasticMQ, so the full path is verified on every dev deploy without running the ECS environment; only the SNS hop is verified in a SWE5001 ECS session.
- This work no longer depends on the service-assembly split (WP-B2/B3): the consumer runs inside the monolith now and inside `notification-svc` later.

## Sub-issues

```
#443 ADR ──┬─ #444 outbox ── #445 relay + ElasticMQ ──┐
           │                                         ├─ #446 consumer ── #448 NFR evidence (CI + ECS session)
           ├─ #215 notification persistence + API ───┤
           │                └─ #449 frontend bell    │
           └─ #447 SWE5001 messaging infra (#376 item 8) ┘
```

- [ ] #443 backend ADR 0007 and backend-constraints amendment
- [x] #215 notification domain, persistence and read API (scope narrowed; event consumption moves to #446)
- [x] #444 transactional outbox and integration event contracts
- [x] #445 outbox relay, SQS/SNS transports, ElasticMQ for local/CI/dev
- [ ] #446 idempotent SQS consumer creating notifications
- [x] #447 SWE5001 messaging infrastructure
- [ ] #448 NFR: reliability and scalability evidence
- [x] ~~#449 frontend notification bell and list~~ (closed as not planned on 2026-10-11)

## Non-goals

- Email, push or WebSocket delivery; FIFO ordering; RabbitMQ, EventBridge, Lambda consumers or CDC (see ADR 0007 alternatives).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On SWE5001 ECS, a team success, team expiry and payment success each produce one notification per recipient, readable through the #215 list endpoint. (The header bell #449 was closed as not planned on 2026-10-11; the EC2 `dev` stack runs no broker.)
- [ ] Duplicate delivery, rollback and poison-message ITs pass in CI against ElasticMQ.
- [ ] On SWE5001 ECS, fan-out, DLQ drill and backlog scaling are captured as evidence before the 2026-10-21 presentation.
- [ ] ADR 0007, NFR register row and SWE5001 plan documents reflect the implemented design.

**Estimate:** about 11–14 ideal developer-days across backend, infrastructure and frontend, plus #215.

> **Rescoped 2026-10-11** (Sprint 4 grade-driven cuts, plan §4 item 8, #465): notifications serve SWE5001 only and rank below the microservice split (plan §4 items 0 and 4). Remaining sprint estimates: #443 3 h, #215 8 h, #444 12 h, #445 10 h, #446 12 h, #447 8 h, #448 4 h.

## Background

A distributed `up` (the promotion run in `swe5001-deploy.yml` and a manual `swe5001-env.yml up`) creates SNS email subscriptions for the notification DLQ and queue-age alarms (#447). Both workflows pass the `swe5001-demo` environment variable `SWE5001_ALERT_EMAIL_ADDRESSES` to Terraform as `TF_VAR_alert_email_addresses`.

Checked on 2026-10-16: the variable is set neither at repository nor at `swe5001-demo` environment level. Without it the promotion fails before any apply:

```text
distributed up requires team alarm recipients in TF_VAR_alert_email_addresses
```

`check_alert_recipients` in `infra/swe5001/scripts/messaging-check.sh` requires **every** listed subscription to be confirmed during the 900-second filter-settle wait, and `runtime` is destroyed after each session, so every recipient receives a new confirmation email in every session (promotion, rehearsal, presentation day). One unconfirmed recipient fails the whole `up`.

Decision (2026-10-16): configure the variable when the `dev` → `prod` promotion PR is merged, not earlier, and list only the operators on duty rather than all five members.

## Scope

1. Just before merging the promotion PR, set the environment variable to a JSON array of the on-duty operators' NUS email addresses (default: @l0sgAi and @PPsyrius; addresses as in the SWE5001 proposal member table):
   ```bash
   gh variable set SWE5001_ALERT_EMAIL_ADDRESSES --repo PPsyrius/iss-groupbuy-team8 --env swe5001-demo --body '["<operator 1>","<operator 2>"]'
   ```
2. Read it back: `gh variable list --repo PPsyrius/iss-groupbuy-team8 --env swe5001-demo`.
3. During the promotion run's 900-second SNS wait, each listed recipient confirms the "AWS Notification - Subscription Confirmation" email (check quarantine and junk folders; NUS Outlook link scanning may confirm or later unsubscribe on its own).
4. For a manual session from a local checkout, export `TF_VAR_alert_email_addresses` with the same JSON array instead; GitHub variables are not read locally.

## Non-goals

- Committing any address to the repository (README "Messaging": recipients are supplied privately).
- Subscribing all five members; others can be added later by changing the variable, effective from the next `up`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `SWE5001_ALERT_EMAIL_ADDRESSES` is set in `swe5001-demo` before the promotion PR is merged.
- [ ] The promotion run passes the routing-readiness gate (`messaging routing and confirmed alarm-recipient readiness passed` in the `up` log); run link recorded in the day log.
- [ ] Recipients and confirmation steps are noted for the 2026-10-20 rehearsal and 2026-10-21 presentation day (presentation guideline and runbook §4).

Refs #447, #448, #456; Sprint 4 container #465.

## Background

The SWE5006 DevSecOps course teaches dynamic application security testing as its own stage of the secure pipeline: DSO 11 (DAST) pp. 2 and 6 name OWASP ZAP, DSO 07.a p. 4 lists DAST beside SAST, and DSO 15 p. 15 places a penetration-test stage after deployment. The pipeline has SAST (SonarCloud gates; CodeQL is opt-in and currently off), SCA (Trivy fs), secret scanning (Gitleaks), IaC scanning (Checkov and Trivy config on `infra/swe5001`) and image scanning (Trivy image), but nothing exercises the *running* application. The SWE5006 deck already admits this gap (`docs/swe5006/presentation/src/content.js`, §3 DevSecOps notes), and report section 4.2 will be asked about it.

The briefing only requires "minimal security considerations", so this should be a light, advisory scan rather than a new merge gate.

## Scope

1. Add `.github/workflows/dast-baseline.yml`: a passive OWASP ZAP baseline scan (`zap-baseline.py`, image pinned by digest) of the dev environment at `vars.FRONTEND_URL_DEV`, for two surfaces: the SPA (`/`) and the backend behind the same CloudFront origin (`/api/v1/products`).
2. Triggers: weekly schedule, manual dispatch (optional base URL), and a PR that edits the workflow itself. No trigger on ordinary PRs, to keep the Actions budget.
3. Upload the HTML/JSON/Markdown reports as artifacts and write the Markdown report to the job summary.
4. Record the new scan and its first findings in `docs/quality/quality-gates.md` (as an advisory, non-gating check), `docs/ci/backend-pipeline.md` and `docs/quality/nfr-register.md`.

## Non-goals

- Active scanning (attack payloads) or authenticated scanning: both could change shared dev data and need a separate decision.
- Making the scan a required check or failing on findings.
- Fixing the findings: each real finding gets its own issue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `actionlint` (the `workflow-lint` job) passes on the new workflow.
- [ ] One successful run on the PR, with both reports attached and the summary listing the alerts.
- [ ] The quality-gate, pipeline and NFR documents describe the scan, its trigger and its advisory status, and list the first run's findings.

## 1 Introduction

### 1.1 Background

- Problem: small merchants can discount only against committed volume, and no single buyer reaches it. "Demand exists, but no buyer commits first" — source: s2 headline M L98 (say C L68: "the discount needs a crowd, and nobody wants to go first"); M L98–102; PROP:25–57 (§4).
- Today's workaround: chat apps and spreadsheets; organisers collect money and refund by hand; sellers have nowhere to post a team price — source: X L35 (SWE5001 s2, same project).
- Mechanism: two prices (solo, team). The leader pays upfront to start a team and shares a link; friends join by paying. If the team fills in time, everyone gets the team price; if it expires, everyone is refunded automatically. Stripe test mode only — source: s2 cue C L69; M L106–112; PROP §4, §6.1.
- Origin of the mechanic: modelled on the early Pinduoduo playbook (proposal §4, 27 Aug) — source: s2 cue C L69; s2 say C L68 ("early Pinduoduo, but for Singapore").
- Technical framing: money is committed before the team exists, so the design is about money safety under concurrency and failure — source: s2 cue C L69.
- Two courses share one repository. SWE5006 system = `dev`, a monolith on one EC2 host behind CloudFront. SWE5001 system = the `prod` branch, three services on ECS. This report describes the SWE5006 system. Production is the shared SWE5001 release: the same code, promoted to `prod` by a code-owner-approved promotion PR (ruleset prod-release); no separate SWE5006 prod stack was built (#226) — source: backend ADR 0008 (`backend/docs/adr/0008-*`, 12 Oct); #465 "Scope decisions"; s9 say/cue C L106–107; s4 say C L78 and Dropped row M L145; s26 say C L224; R 4.4 (team ruling 25 Oct).
- Project status at submission, in one paragraph pointing to §2.2:
  - four sprints run, Sprint 4 ended 23 Oct; Sprint 4 tag v0.1.0-sprint4 on fba3cfbd, cut by Pan 24 Oct — source: #465; `DoD:41–56`; s5 M L179;
  - Sprint 4 placed at released: production on ECS through the shared SWE5001 release (17 and 20 Oct, Stripe test mode); dev shows paid start, a second buyer's join and the refund, 23–24 Oct; the team re-agreed this placement on #619 (25 Oct) — source: s7 Sprint 4 row M L213; s7 say C L94; s5 milestone M L172; 7a160495;
  - UC1–UC9 issues closed as completed, 19–28 Sep — source: #24–#32 (gh); M L143;
  - paid START and the expiry refund shown on dev 23 Oct; the repair merged 24 Oct — source: PR #664 (bef39b72, merged 2026-10-24 06:53 UTC); `backend/docs/payment/stripe-dev-recovery-acceptance-20261023.md`; C L79;
  - a second buyer's paid JOIN shown on dev 24 Oct (system demo backup recording: "2 of 2 joined · Filled 24 Oct, 7:17 pm"); Yorik closed #517, #223 and #590 on 25 Oct; still not shown on dev: crash recovery under replay (#224, open) — source: #657; s4 cue C L79; s4 Open row M L144.

- Do not reuse `README.md:140–221`: it describes "organisers" and predates the pay-first model — source: #463 audit comment (Eric, 22 Oct); R2 §1.1.

### 1.2 Business Needs

- Merchants: sell at a discount only against committed, prepaid volume — source: s2 headline M L98; PROP:44–50.
- Buyers: reach a bulk price together without trusting an organiser with money — source: M L100–102; X L35.
- Platform: no manual collection or refunds; each payment, refund and transition is auditable — source: PROP:44–50; PROP §6.3 auditability (s3 table M L118–125).
- Drivers stated per use case: a dual price so buyers see the saving (#24); pay-first initiation (#26); a safe last-seat join (#27); an automatic, idempotent, auditable refund on expiry (#29); attributed invite links (#30) — source: issue bodies (gh 24 Oct; R3 §1.2).
- Design drivers from the proposal: maintainability and extensibility, quoted: "new pricing schemes, payment providers, and team-resolution consequences must be addable without modifying existing domain logic" — source: PROP §6.3 (PROP:302–326); s32 cue C L287.

### 1.3 Stakeholders

Use a table with columns stakeholder, kind (business/IT/external), interest, and how the project serves it.

- Buyer as team leader (starts and pays first) and as joiner (pays to join, possibly via invite) — source: s12 use-case actors C L121–122; demo accounts "Leader", "Joiner" C L258; use-case.svg actor "Buyer".
- Small merchant: benefits from committed volume. There is no merchant GUI; merchant self-service is out of scope — source: PROP:44–50; PROP §6.2 (use-case.svg out-of-scope package).
- Platform administrator: manages listings and team terms (UC9, admin console) — source: #32; #221; frontend ADR 0015; use-case.svg actor "Admin".
- External systems as secondary actors: Stripe (Checkout, refunds, webhooks; test mode) and Google (sign-in) — source: s12 cue C L122; use-case.svg.

# Report plan: chapter 3, sections 3.1–3.3

Owners: 3.1 Liu Jin; 3.2 Eric and Yorik (halves); 3.3 Lim (#463). Legend and decisions: the [plan index on #463](https://github.com/PPsyrius/iss-groupbuy-team8/issues/463#issuecomment-6381866294).
Deck citations below (sN, BN, C/M/B Lnnn) are to the deck (PR #683, 7b1e7657) unless marked 064446f9.

## 3.1 Software Architecture

The template asks for UML diagrams of the components (if distributed) and of the logical layers and packages, plus the target platform (TPL L60–61, course). Scope decision D10: this section describes the SWE5006 monolith.

**Logical architecture**
- Modular monolith in the COLA style: four layers (adapter, application, domain, infrastructure), with each bounded context a package in every layer — source: s9 say C L106; M L326–338; TS:9; `backend-skeleton-plan.md` D1 (30 Aug).
- Maven modules: blocbuy-client, -domain, -application, -adapter, -infrastructure, -bootstrap, plus blocbuy-platform (SWE5001 assembly, unused by the monolith) and `backend/services/{identity,commerce,notification}-svc` (SWE5001) — source: `backend/pom.xml:22–32`; TS:51–61.
- Dependency rule: adapter → application → domain; infrastructure → domain; domain depends on the JDK and Lombok only — source: `backend-skeleton-plan.md` §4.
- Bounded contexts: catalog, groupbuy, identity, notification, order, payment, plus common. Invites and credits live inside groupbuy — source: `backend-skeleton-plan.md` D4; s9 cue C L107; R4 §3.1.
- Per-context domain packages `model/ repository/ gateway/ event/` — source: `backend/blocbuy-domain/src/main/java/com/blocbuy/` (R4 §3.1).
- Ports and adapters:
  - 20 domain repository ports — source: R4 §3.1 (`*/repository/` count);
  - gateway ports, e.g. `CheckoutGateway`, `RefundGateway`, `OAuthIdentityGateway`, `RateLimitGateway`, `OutboxEventTransport`, implemented in infrastructure by `StripeCheckoutGateway`, `GoogleOAuthGateway`, `RedisRateLimitGateway`, `Sns/SqsOutboxEventTransport` — source: R4 §3.1;
  - two domain ports implemented in application: `PaymentBusinessPort` ← `OrderFulfilmentAdapter`, and `PaymentIntentPort` ← `PurchaseIntentAppService` — source: `backend/blocbuy-application/.../order/service/OrderFulfilmentAdapter.java`; s9 cue C L107.
- Enforcement: 17 ArchUnit rules, named in a table (e.g. `domain_is_framework_free`, `application_uses_ports_not_tech`, `controllers_never_touch_persistence`, `no_field_injection`, `controllers_are_validated`, `commerce_reaches_identity_only_through_user_port`) — source: `backend/blocbuy-bootstrap/src/test/java/com/blocbuy/architecture/ArchitectureTest.java:67` (R4 §3.1).
- API surface:
  - 14 `@RestController` classes (InternalUserController in the distributed topology only) plus 2 advice classes — source: R4 §3.1; s9 cue C L107;
  - `contracts/openapi.json`: 27 paths, 31 operations, under `/api/v1` — source: R4 §3.1; `backend-skeleton-plan.md` D11–D12;
  - one `Result<T>` envelope, success code `COMMON_200_000` — source: frontend ADR 0009; TS:13.
- Frontend: pure client-side SPA on S3 + CloudFront; same-origin `/api` cookie session; router owns URL state; generated client — source: frontend ADRs 0001, 0002, 0003, 0004, 0005, 0007 (`frontend/docs/adr/README.md`).
- Architectural decisions, summarised as a table: decision | ADR or D-number | date — source: M L325; `backend/docs/adr/README.md` (0001 22 Sep … 0008 12 Oct); `frontend/docs/adr/README.md` (0001–0015).
  - Modular monolith (D1, D4).
  - Framework-free domain (D1, no ADR).
  - Consequences before commit (ADR 0002).
  - Referral credit after commit (ADR 0003).
  - Outbox to SNS/SQS (ADR 0007, file status "Proposed"; R4 C3).
  - One codebase, two topologies (ADR 0008).
  - GAP: decisions without an ADR (MyBatis, Sa-Token, scheduling, concurrency approach) → Appendix B, owner Liu Jin (OI 7; TS:17).

**Target implementation platform**: a table of layer | technology | version | source.
- Backend: Java 21; Spring Boot 4.1.1; MyBatis; Sa-Token 1.46 (Redis session); Flyway; stripe-java (infrastructure only); springdoc; ArchUnit; Testcontainers — source: `backend/pom.xml`; s9 cue C L107; R4 §3.1.

- Frontend: React 19.3.1, TanStack Router 1.170.44, Query 5.104.3, Form 1.33.5, TypeScript 7.0.2, Vite 8.3.4, HeroUI 3.2.6, Tailwind 4.3.3, Valibot 1.5.0, hey-api openapi-ts, Vitest 5.0.1, Playwright 1.64.1 — source: `frontend/package.json` (R4 §3.1; deck read 23 Oct).

Show it here as the component view of the SWE5006 system (D10) and reuse it in §4.3 — source: `dev-deployment.svg` (F17; stereotypes read 24 Oct).

The deck now says it in s9 ("The same code also runs as three services on AWS", C L106, 12a33e80) and frames that SWE5001 release as the production environment, promoted by an approved PR (s26 say C L224, 0fcbe7d6).

## 3.2 Transition from Analysis to Design

The template asks for the strategies that guide a designer end to end. For each: impacted analysis objects, impacted use cases, typical class changes with rationale, and typical sequence changes with rationale (TPL L63–65, course).

**3.2 overview** (owner Eric)
- System shape and the decisions taken as given (Java 21/Spring Boot 4.1, React 19, `/api/v1` JSON with one envelope, PostgreSQL via MyBatis, database locks) — source: TS:7–15.
- Strategy table: strategy | concern | written yes/no. Nine rows; five written — source: TS:19–31; s10 M L341–351.
- Four strategies without an ADR (language/framework, persistence, scheduling job, concurrency) — source: TS:17; s10 cue C L112.
- UC4 analysis → design mapping, seven rows (JoinTeamUI, PaymentGateway, JoinTeamControl, Team+Membership, Order, Payment, Refund) — source: TS:33–45; backup B17 (moved from s12 in ad3e814c; M L376–384), cue at 064446f9 C L120 (deleted at HEAD).
- Typical class change: GUI «boundary» → route + component + Query hook + generated client; «control» → `@RestController` + application service; «entity» → aggregate behind a domain repository port with a MyBatis mapper; external «boundary» → gateway port + adapter — source: s11 M L361; cue C L118.
- Typical sequence change: control → `entity.update()` becomes service → `repository.lockDeal()` (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) → `aggregate.joinPaid()` → guarded UPDATE, all in one transaction — source: M L368–371; `PaidGroupDealMapper.xml:25,33,73`.
- Rationale: dependency inversion; the domain names its needs as interfaces — source: M L372; C L116–118.
- Mechanisms that are not GoF patterns (Repository/DAO, outbox, idempotency keys, Optimistic Offline Lock) are named as such — source: QA§2 C L315.
- Figures: `transition-pair.svg` (backup B17, F2); `uc4-analysis-class.svg` and `uc4-design-class.svg` are cross-referenced to §3.4.1 — source: deck diagrams.

## 3.5.5 Listing rules that depend on its state: State, with Optimistic Offline Lock, by Liu Jin — status: partial (deck has all parts; no text)

## 3.6 Database Schemas (owner Liu Jin) — status: partial (diagrams ready, no text)

The template asks for suitable diagrams of the schema(s) (TPL L88, course).

**Schema facts**
- One PostgreSQL 18 database on dev, schema `domain`; Flyway V1–V28 (28 SQL files plus `V23…sql.conf` for CONCURRENTLY); repeatable seed `db/seed/R__demo_catalog_seed.sql` — source: git ls-tree OD `backend/blocbuy-bootstrap/src/main/resources/db/migration` (24 Oct); R4 §3.6.
- V1 rules: snake_case, `timestamptz`, `numeric` money — source: B4 B L78–86.
- 29 tables by context — source: R4 §3.6 list; B4 B L78–86:
  - identity: `sys_user`, `sys_user_oauth`, `sys_role`, `sys_permission`, `rel_user_role`, `rel_role_permission`; V3, V24;
  - catalog: `biz_product`, `biz_team_price_policy`, `biz_team_price_quote`, `log_product_team_terms`; V4, V6, V14, V20, V21;
  - groupbuy: `biz_group_deal`, `biz_group_member`, `biz_group_participation_receipt`, `biz_share_invite`, `biz_share_credit`; V5, V7, V18;
  - order: `biz_order`, `biz_purchase_intent`; V12, V15, V19, V22;
  - payment: `biz_payment`, `log_payment_webhook_event`, `biz_refund`, `log_payment_review`, `biz_payment_review_case`, `log_refund_attempt`; V2, V9–V11, V16;
  - notification: `biz_notification`, `sys_consumed_message`; V27, V28;
  - jobs and outbox: `sys_outbox`, `sys_scheduler_lock`, `sys_scheduled_item_retry`, `sys_checkout_expiry_cursor`; V13, V17, V25, V26.
- Source-of-truth DDL per context — source: `backend/docs/db/{catalog,catalog-team-price,groupbuy,identity,notification,order,payment}.sql` (R4 §3.6).

**Mapping decisions**
- UUIDv7 surrogate PKs (`uuid DEFAULT uuidv7()`), except `sys_consumed_message` PK(event_id, consumer) — source: R4 §3.6; s19 M L526–532.
- No FOREIGN KEY or CHECK constraints anywhere (grep = 0). Relationships are logical, enforced by the application and unique indexes. This is a team DDL rule, not a course rule — source: `V5__groupbuy.sql:2`; `.claude/skills/pgsql-ddl/SKILL.md`; SAD 04a p55 (cited at C L157).
  - Reason (not performance): on the SWE5001 ECS environment each service has its own database on the shared RDS instance (backend ADR 0008, Data), so a cross-service link such as `biz_group_deal.leader_user_id` → `sys_user` cannot be a foreign key; ADR 0001's START reserves its `deal_id` before the team row exists; one schema is kept for both environments, so consistency moves into the application — source: s19 cue C L157 (deck (PR #683, 7b1e7657)); 5174c717.
- Unique indexes as race backstops: `uq_biz_group_member_deal_user`, `biz_refund_payment_id_key`, `uq_biz_payment_request_key` (Checkout idempotency), `uq_log_payment_webhook_event_event_id` — source: s15 cue C L137; s19 cue C L157; R4 ERD table.
- One table per aggregate root; no inheritance mapping (SAD 04a p53–61) — source: s19 crop caption M L529 (deck (PR #683, 7b1e7657)).
- `biz_purchase_intent` has no status column; `biz_group_deal.version` is incremented but not compared — source: s15 cue C L137; s19 cue C L157.
- Orphan rows: application checks; deleted flag; `AdminListingAppServiceImpl.delete` → `PRODUCT_REFERENCED`; the Q&A answer now adds the reason: in the cloud each service has its own database (ADR 0008), so a link to another service's table cannot be a foreign key anyway — source: QA§2 C L318 (deck (PR #683, 7b1e7657)).
- Indexes that serve the jobs: `idx_biz_group_deal_status_expire` (V5:55); `idx_biz_refund_due` (V16:15); V23 CONCURRENTLY indexes; `idx_sys_outbox_unpublished` (V26:20) — source: R4 §3.6.

**Tables and figures**
- Core-entity table: entity | PK | logical FK columns | unique keys | cardinality, 17 rows — source: R4 "ERD core-entity table".
- Figure: core ERD, 8 tables (`biz_product`, `biz_group_deal`, `biz_group_member`, `biz_purchase_intent`, `biz_payment`, `biz_order`, `biz_refund`, `sys_user`) — `src/diagrams/core-erd.svg` (deck s19, F15).
- Figure: full ERD, 29 tables, in Appendix C — `src/diagrams/full-erd.svg` (F21, B16).
- SWE5001 note: one RDS instance, one database per service, roles granted only their own tables — source: ADR 0008 (table ownership); `blocbuy-platform` `db/swe5001/afterMigrate__service_grants.sql`; QA§2 C L317.
  - GAP: a per-service ownership diagram exists only as text. Optional for this report — owner Liu Jin.

## 4.1 Source Control Strategy

The template asks for project structure, repository strategy, branching strategy and developer authentication (TPL L91, course).

**Project structure and repository**
- One private monorepo `PPsyrius/iss-groupbuy-team8`, default branch `dev` — source: gh api repos (24 Oct).
- Top-level layout as a table: dir | holds — source: `git ls-tree origin/dev` (24 Oct); s22 cue C L190.

- History: 502 commits on dev since 24 Aug; 412 PRs merged into dev — source: R5 §4.1 (gh, 24 Oct).

**Branching strategy**

Part of #463 (SWE5006 final report, due **31 Oct 2026 23:59**). Report sections: §4 DevSecOps (#680) and appendices (#681). **Blocked by #610.**

## Background

The final report should show our OWASP ZAP scan results before and after remediation. @PPsyrius provides the artefacts and @limjiechao puts them in the report.

- **Before:** the first passive baseline of dev, [run 39733450177](https://github.com/PPsyrius/iss-groupbuy-team8/actions/runs/39733450177) (#606, 22 Oct). Findings: 0 High, 2 Medium, 4 Low, 6 Informational. Each finding has its own issue, #636–#647. The `zap-web` and `zap-api` artifacts **expire on 21 Nov 2026** (30-day retention).
- **Latest clean run without remediation:** [run 40298983391](https://github.com/PPsyrius/iss-groupbuy-team8/actions/runs/40298983391) (scheduled, 26 Oct, success). It has the same findings as the first baseline.
- **After:** no run exists yet. The response-headers fix is #610, still open.

## Scope

**Pan (provide)**
1. Close #610 by fixing each finding or accepting it with a reason, then dispatch `dast-baseline` on `dev`.
2. Download `zap-web` and `zap-api` from the before run and the after run (`gh run download <run-id>`). Attach the HTML reports to this issue, or put them in the shared report folder.
3. Post a delta table as a comment here:

   | ZAP rule | Risk | Issue | Before | After | Outcome (fixed / accepted + reason) |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Lim (include)**
4. Add the delta table and a short summary to §4 (#680), with run IDs and dates.
5. Add the full before/after reports, or excerpts from them, as a report appendix (#681).

## Non-goals

- Active or authenticated ZAP scans. #610 does not include them either.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An after run exists on `dev`, run after #610 merged, and is linked here.
- [ ] Before and after reports saved outside GitHub Actions retention.
- [ ] Delta table posted, covering every finding in #636–#647.
- [ ] §4 and the appendix carry the table and the reports.

**Fallback:** if #610 is not done by 29 Oct, the report shows the before run and the accepted-risk reasons, and states plainly that the remediation is pending.

## References

- #606, #610, #636–#647, #680, #681, #682 (ZAP beta-rules pin)
- `.github/workflows/dast-baseline.yml`, `docs/quality/quality-gates.md` (NFR-71)
